How you end up paying too much

Many phone plans being offered by large telecommunications companies like AT&T and Verizon offer customers installment plans to slowly pay off their device over time. You should never, ever do this if you’re serious about saving money. Why? If you keep a smartphone even for even two or three years, you still keep paying some kind of installment fee. You keep paying it even after the phone is paid off.

I've always thought this should be obvious but the amount of people who don't know is staggering.

$45 a month also seems ridiculous to me, especially for a single phone.

The price per monthincreases the more data you want. They screw poor people who balk at the price of the outright cost of a new phone on the mobile data costs, then they rely on users either switching up to a newer phone after 2 years or keep paying that new phone tax forever. They never tell people about the BYO phone plans that cost half as much, that come with 8 times the data STANDARD compared to a new phone and plan. They are scum.
Yup, once I found out about BLU, I was fucking sold instantly.

It's never obvious, at least partly because phone companies deliberately obfuscate their offerings and pricing structures specifically to make it hard to compare plans.

To figure it out, you need to take into account:

  • Whether or not you actually need/want a new phone, and if so what model you want
  • How much that phone costs to purchase separate from a plan, and how much it costs as part of a plan
  • What level of mobile service you actually require
  • What that level of service costs as a BYO-phone service, and what it costs as part of a bundle

Example 1:

New handset needed, I wanted a Nexus 5, and I needed a specific phone provider due to their exclusive remote-area coverage. Free market cost for the phone was ~$500, and the minimum cost for a basic BYO plan with the provider I needed to use was $50/mo. Total cost for BYO phone plus service for two years: $1700. The same phone bundled with better plan on a two year contract was $69/month, total cost: $1656. So in this case the bundle was cheaper overall, and got me a better level of service for 'free'.

Example 2:

Nexus 5 finally died, upgraded to Nexus 5X. Minimum cost for a plan with bundled 5X was around $1800. Meanwhile the provider had introduced a $35/mo BYO plan which still met my needs, and I could source a 5X online for $460. Total cost for BYO phone plus service for two years: $1300. In this case buying separately and using the BYO plan saves me $250/year.
